validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) on WebFetch, and wiki_citations.json is empty for this row per the scope note, so there were no sheet-cited sources to re-check -- this was ground-up open-web research. The row's [ref] set was completely empty (all 8 units MISSING_REF), so the first question was existence: is 'HQ2-Tando Adam Gas Pipeline' a real, independently-documented SSGC line, or a GEM-only/hallucinated entity? It is real. Two independent Government of Pakistan documents name this exact segment: (1) the Ministry of Energy Petroleum Division / PPIS 'Investment Brochure' gas-transmission-network schematic map (ppisonline.com), which labels a segment '24"x81KM HQ2-TANDO ADAM SECTION' -- diameter and length match GEM's 24 in / 81 km exactly; (2) OGRA's 'State of [the] Regulated Industry' report, Table 3.21 'SSGCL's Capacity Utilization of Transmission Network' (source cited in the report as SSGCL), which lists a row '24'' Dia.X 84 Km HQ2-TandoAdam' with Available Capacity of 85 MMCFD as of both June 30 2019 and June 30 2020 -- capacity matches GEM's 85.00 MMcf/d exactly, diameter matches (24 in), but length is stated as 84 km, not 81 km. This is a genuine cross-source disagreement (81 vs 84 km, ~3.6%), not a GEM error vs. a single correct source -- I found no third source to break the tie, so I'm flagging rather than silently keeping GEM's 81 km. Both documents also confirm classification (OGRA's table sits under section 3.3.3 'SSGCL Transmission infrastructure' / heading 'NATURAL GAS', i.e. this is unambiguously a gas transmission segment, matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas) and ownership (OGRA table explicitly sourced '(Source: SSGCL)' i.e. Sui Southern Gas Company, matching GEM's Owner1=Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100%). Status=operating is inferred from context, not a literal statement: the OGRA table reports nonzero Available Capacity for this named segment in two consecutive fiscal years (FY19, FY20), i.e. it is treated as a live, in-service part of SSGCL's transmission network in that regulatory filing (the report separately notes segment-level utilization % 'could not be calculated due to integrated transmission network', so I did not try to force a literal utilization figure). No duplicate risk within the 63-row roster: the two OGRA-table neighbours 'Masu-HQ3' (24"x15km, cap 40) and the 'Tando Adam to Masu' loopline (24"x34km, cap 23) are genuinely distinct adjoining SSGC segments, and neither appears elsewhere in the roster under another name, so P4017 is not a relabel of another tracked row. Minor attribution caveat (not escalated to its own concern): GEM's StartLocation is 'Nawabshah', but the segment's actual named origin per both sources is the 'HQ2' station/node, not the town of Nawabshah itself -- on the PPIS schematic, HQ2 sits in the same corridor cluster as a '...N.Shah-...NAWABSHAH' label (alongside other HQ2-linked segments: 42"x82km Nara-HQ2, 24"x16km HQ2-KA, 42"x50km Lundo HQ2-Nara), which is consistent with GEM's town-level simplification but is not a literal confirmation that HQ2 is coincident with Nawabshah town proper; EndLocation='Tando Adam' is solidly confirmed since it's literally in the segment's name in both sources.
